sinks.name: TA_InvokeCommandEntryPoint
sinks.reason: May carry per-session sensitive state used to authorize or process commands.

sinks.name: TA_InvokeCommandEntryPoint
sinks.reason: Controls which command handler executes; affects security-relevant control flow.

sinks.name: TA_InvokeCommandEntryPoint
sinks.reason: Determines how input/output parameters are interpreted and validated.

sinks.name: TA_InvokeCommandEntryPoint
sinks.reason: Carries client-supplied inputs and receives outputs; likely read/written/transformed by the TA.

sinks.name: TA_OpenSessionEntryPoint
sinks.reason: typically carries client identity/connection metadata that may be read/validated to authorize a session

sinks.name: TA_OpenSessionEntryPoint
sinks.reason: commonly contains client-provided values and buffers that the TA reads/writes/validates when opening a session

sinks.name: TEE_AllocateTransientObject
sinks.reason: Determines what kind of cryptographic/key object is allocated, influencing how sensitive material may be stored/handled.

sinks.name: TEE_AllocateTransientObject
sinks.reason: Controls the size/capacity of the transient object, affecting allocation and subsequent handling of sensitive key/material.

sinks.name: TEE_AllocateTransientObject
sinks.reason: Receives a handle to a newly created transient object that will hold sensitive data (e.g., keys) and may be used in later security operations.

sinks.name: TEE_DigestDoFinal
sinks.reason: Selects the digest context/state used to process input and produce output

sinks.name: TEE_DigestDoFinal
sinks.reason: Buffer contents are read and hashed (security-relevant transformation)

sinks.name: TEE_DigestDoFinal
sinks.reason: Controls how many bytes from the input buffer are read

sinks.name: TEE_DigestDoFinal
sinks.reason: Receives the computed digest (security-relevant output write)

sinks.name: TEE_DigestDoFinal
sinks.reason: Determines available output size and is updated with actual digest length

sinks.name: TEE_DigestUpdate
sinks.reason: buffer contents are read and incorporated into the ongoing digest state

sinks.name: TEE_InitRefAttribute
sinks.reason: receives references to caller-provided data buffer and length, influencing later cryptographic/object operations
sinks.role: output attribute structure to be initialized

sinks.name: TEE_InitRefAttribute
sinks.reason: pointer to potentially sensitive material (e.g., key/IV/nonce) that will be associated with the attribute
sinks.role: input data buffer referenced by the attribute

sinks.name: TEE_InitRefAttribute
sinks.reason: controls how much data is referenced; affects bounds/semantics of subsequent use

sinks.name: TEE_MACCompareFinal

sinks.name: TEE_MACCompareFinal
sinks.reason: Buffer contents are read and incorporated into the MAC computation before final comparison

sinks.name: TEE_MACCompareFinal
sinks.reason: Controls how many bytes from the message buffer are read/processed

sinks.name: TEE_MACCompareFinal
sinks.reason: Buffer is read and compared against the computed MAC value (authentication check)

sinks.name: TEE_MACCompareFinal
sinks.reason: Controls how many bytes from the expected tag buffer are read/compared

sinks.name: TEE_MACComputeFinal
sinks.reason: Identifies the ongoing MAC computation context containing key/material and accumulated state

sinks.name: TEE_MACComputeFinal
sinks.reason: Reads caller-provided data to be authenticated as part of the MAC computation

sinks.name: TEE_MACComputeFinal
sinks.reason: Controls how many bytes are read from the input buffer

sinks.name: TEE_MACComputeFinal
sinks.reason: Writes the computed MAC/tag output, which is security-sensitive derived data

sinks.name: TEE_MACComputeFinal
sinks.reason: Determines output size and may be updated with actual MAC length, affecting how much is written

sinks.name: TEE_MACInit

sinks.name: TEE_MACInit
sinks.reason: Provides cryptographic IV/nonce bytes that influence MAC computation and must be treated as security-relevant input

sinks.name: TEE_MACInit
sinks.reason: Controls how many bytes of the IV/nonce are read from memory, affecting cryptographic processing

sinks.name: TEE_MemMove

sinks.name: TEE_MemMove
sinks.reason: provides bytes to be copied; reads potentially sensitive data

sinks.name: TEE_MemMove
sinks.reason: controls amount of data moved; impacts how much is read/written and potential overflows

sinks.name: TEE_PopulateTransientObject
sinks.reason: receives populated sensitive attributes/keys, affecting cryptographic object state

sinks.name: TEE_PopulateTransientObject
sinks.reason: contains attribute values (e.g., key material) that are read and imported into the object

sinks.name: TEE_PopulateTransientObject
sinks.reason: controls how many attributes are read from the array, influencing parsing/import behavior

sinks.name: TEE_SetOperationKey
sinks.reason: The operation state is modified to use a specific key, affecting subsequent security-sensitive cryptographic processing.
sinks.role: cryptographic operation handle (destination for key material association)

sinks.name: TEE_SetOperationKey
sinks.reason: Provides/identifies the cryptographic key material that will be bound to the operation, which is security-critical data.
